principles.name: separation in space
principles.heuristic: Let each opposing requirement hold in a different component, node, region, layer, partition, namespace, or architectural location.

principles.name: separation in time
principles.heuristic: Let each opposing requirement hold at a different time, phase, transaction stage, deployment window, operating mode, or lifecycle state.

principles.name: separation in relation (condition/context)
principles.heuristic: Let the same element satisfy opposite properties for different users, requests, tenants, relationships, contexts, modes, workloads, or other operating conditions.

principles.name: separation in system level
principles.heuristic: Place one required property at the whole-system or supersystem level and the opposing property at a subsystem, component, instance, or lower abstraction level.

principles.name: satisfying contradictory demands
principles.heuristic: Change state, representation, protocol, parameters, or mechanism so both opposing requirements can hold simultaneously rather than being separated.

principles.name: bypassing contradictory demands
principles.heuristic: Redesign the workflow, interaction, architecture, or system boundary so the conflicted parameter or requirement becomes irrelevant instead of being optimized.
